chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from some of our companions, from one of them, peace be upon them, who said:
Wrapping the garment over the shoulders above the tawashshuḥ in salat (prayer) is disliked, and performing tawashshuḥ over the qamīṣ is disliked.
My qamīṣ in salat (prayer)? So he said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.التَّوَشُّحِ: wrapping oneself in a garment in a particular manner
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat (prayer) in which these dress rulings apply
key_terms.الِارْتِدَاءُ: wearing or draping a garment over the shoulders
key_terms.الْقَمِيصِ: a shirt or tunic worn during salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it; it is permissible
key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: disliked; not forbidden but better to avoid

ai.seo_question: What kinds of clothing arrangements are disliked or permissible in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding forms of dress in salat (prayer). It states that certain ways of wrapping garments are makruh (disliked), while wearing a qamīṣ in salat (prayer) is permissible and unobjectionable.
